findings.reason: the memo key must carry the exemption inputs (`node.role` and `node.id`, or the exemption verdict itself) as well as the section, and case 2's fixture must queue a review-role and an implement request on one section, otherwise the node ships a coverage memo that silently reads the wrong answer for the one request the gate is for.
findings.text: the deliverable says the dispatch-gate fallback "is memoized in the same record, keyed additionally by the section the request builds", but `_dispatch_gate_owed` (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:3216`) calls `routing.require_plan_reviewed`, whose verdict is decided by `_plan_review_exempt(node)` — true for `role` in `{"investigate","review","test"}` or for a node id that `_is_review_node` reads as a reviewer (`reckon/crew/routing.py:2420,2454-2468`) — as well as by `plan_review_units(node.section)`; a plan's own review request and the implement request it exists to unblock are routinely queued on the same plan and section at the same time, so a section-only key makes whichever is judged first the answer for both — an exempt review request's `None` is reused for the implement request and the plan-review gate fails open, which is the exact class of shortcut the unit says it will not build

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited module and symbol resolves (`_plan_review_owed` at 3244, `_section_digests` at 3319, `read_state_file` at 3328, the document-contract check at 3329–3337, `advance_waiting_requests` and `_release_plan_review_holds` at 3683–3684 inside `admit_once`); the fallback returns sit at 3302 and 3316 against the unit's "near lines 3315 and 3325", which is line drift only, and the extensionless `a-read-costs-what-changed` href resolves as `.html`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — case 2 of the five counts `routing.require_plan_reviewed` "once per section those requests build", but that gate's verdict also varies by `node.role` and `node.id` (`reckon/crew/routing.py:2454-2468`), so the key the measure asserts is not the key the gate reads; the four declared controls otherwise map correctly onto cases 1, 2, 3 and 5, and case 4 is covered only indirectly by the third control.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the timing arm lands under the run's own `logs/` directory, which is durable under `~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/<run>/`, not a scratchpad; the unit test writes no external state.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test file and record are named for what they do, and no plan label, stage name or ticket number reaches a symbol or a comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the dispatch-gate fallback is memoized "keyed additionally by the section the request builds", but `require_plan_reviewed` answers differently for two requests on one plan and one section that differ in role or node id, so the memo can hand an exempt review node's `None` to an implement request and switch the gate off.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s4 names two mechanisms (the per-plan review-read record and the `waits_seconds` stage split), but one done-when with five cases and one named test file closes both on one verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s4's declared `depends-on` (`a-read-costs-what-changed#s6`) resolves: `docs/plans/a-read-costs-what-changed.html` exists and carries s1–s7, and s4 names no relationship it does not need.
